pubcol-w-ca95faac88640390.definition_en: to start learning to play a musical instrument as a new hobby or activity
collocations: take up a musical instrument later in life
decide to take up an instrument
pubcol-w-ca95faac88640390.example_simple: She decided to take up a musical instrument and chose the guitar.
pubcol-w-ca95faac88640390.example_complex: Many adults who take up a musical instrument later in life find that it sharpens their memory and relieves stress.

pubcol-w-b4afe6a51ec6f45e.definition_en: to begin doing physical activity regularly as a habit
collocations: take up exercise to lose weight
encourage someone to take up exercise
pubcol-w-b4afe6a51ec6f45e.example_simple: My doctor advised me to take up exercise to improve my health.
pubcol-w-b4afe6a51ec6f45e.example_complex: After years of a sedentary lifestyle, he finally took up exercise and gradually built the stamina to run a marathon.

pubcol-w-2a817a71df67e501.definition_en: to accept that you are in charge of something and will be blamed if it goes wrong
pubcol-w-2a817a71df67e501.example_simple: As team leader, she had to take responsibility for the project's results.
pubcol-w-2a817a71df67e501.example_complex: The minister publicly assumed responsibility for the failures of his department rather than blaming his subordinates.

pubcol-w-86f12bd6277b0f55.definition_en: to accept that you are answerable for something and its consequences
pubcol-w-86f12bd6277b0f55.example_simple: He agreed to take responsibility for the broken window.
pubcol-w-86f12bd6277b0f55.example_complex: No one was willing to assume responsibility for the budget shortfall, so the investigation dragged on for months.

collocations: take a glance at the menu
cast a glance at the clock
pubcol-w-c9ac27e3efd87b91.example_simple: She took a glance at her phone during the meeting.
pubcol-w-c9ac27e3efd87b91.example_complex: He cast a nervous glance at the examiner before turning over the paper and beginning the test.

pubcol-w-7345bbdfddac940d.definition_en: to be tested formally on a subject by answering questions under exam conditions
pubcol-w-7345bbdfddac940d.example_simple: I have to take an exam next Monday.
pubcol-w-7345bbdfddac940d.example_complex: Candidates who wish to study abroad must sit an English proficiency exam before they can apply to most universities.

pubcol-w-f6b14d8359a44d41.example_simple: I take a bus to school every morning.
pubcol-w-f6b14d8359a44d41.example_complex: Rather than sitting in traffic, commuters are increasingly choosing to take a bus that runs in a dedicated lane.

pubcol-w-da46ca6c95bc4a33.definition_en: to do something in order to deal with a problem or achieve a result
pubcol-w-da46ca6c95bc4a33.example_simple: We must take action to reduce plastic waste.
pubcol-w-da46ca6c95bc4a33.example_complex: Unless governments take urgent action on emissions, scientists warn that the effects of climate change will soon be irreversible.

pubcol-w-e8a363b3db8e601a.definition_en: to sit down (often said politely as an invitation)
collocations: take a seat in the waiting room
take a seat at the table
pubcol-w-e8a363b3db8e601a.example_simple: Please take a seat while the doctor gets ready.
pubcol-w-e8a363b3db8e601a.example_complex: The receptionist smiled and asked us to take a seat until our name was called for the interview.

pubcol-w-bbcb9fd2fd347a00.definition_en: to become interested in or pay attention to something
pubcol-w-bbcb9fd2fd347a00.example_simple: She takes a great interest in painting.
pubcol-w-bbcb9fd2fd347a00.example_complex: Good managers take a genuine interest in their employees' development rather than focusing solely on output.

e1b8debc-11f1-4d47-83ff-39fea058bfe2.definition_en: to interfere with or alter something without permission, usually to cause damage or gain an advantage

pubcol-w-3330ed719152b09e.example_simple: His silence was tantamount to admitting he was guilty.
pubcol-w-3330ed719152b09e.example_complex: The committee argued that ignoring the warnings was tantamount to negligence, and demanded a full investigation.

pubcol-w-e799c3668f4b1c33.definition_en: the kind of music that a person likes and prefers
pubcol-w-e799c3668f4b1c33.example_simple: We have the same taste in music, so we always agree on playlists.
pubcol-w-e799c3668f4b1c33.example_complex: Her taste in music is remarkably eclectic, ranging from baroque concertos to underground electronic tracks.

pubcol-w-817967366c6796d1.definition_en: a student who is treated as a favourite by the teacher, often disliked by classmates for it
pubcol-w-817967366c6796d1.example_simple: Everyone called him the teacher's pet because he always got the best marks.
pubcol-w-817967366c6796d1.example_complex: She resented being labelled the teacher's pet, since her good grades came from hard work rather than any special favour.

b2376f72-b63e-4bd9-863a-75e78af75cde.definition_en: a hospital connected to a medical school where students are trained while patients are treated

pubcol-w-d25187dc137f35c8.definition_en: a group of people who work or play together towards a shared goal
pubcol-w-d25187dc137f35c8.example_simple: Our team won the football match yesterday.
pubcol-w-d25187dc137f35c8.example_complex: A well-coordinated team can achieve far more than a group of talented individuals working in isolation.

pubcol-w-54c4f31b224078c0.example_simple: Filling in the forms was a tedious job.
pubcol-w-54c4f31b224078c0.example_complex: Although the research involved months of tedious data entry, the eventual findings proved well worth the effort.

pubcol-w-7a49c995a63bc18a.example_simple: He has been teetotal since his twenties and never touches alcohol.
pubcol-w-7a49c995a63bc18a.example_complex: Having grown up in a teetotal family, she found the heavy drinking culture at university genuinely bewildering.

pubcol-w-d69e57cfad112101.definition_en: to recognise the difference between two or more similar people or things

pubcol-w-d69e57cfad112101.example_complex: The imitations were so skilfully made that even experts struggled to tell the forgeries apart from the originals.

pubcol-w-964e4c3f047fcece.example_simple: Can you tell the difference between these two colours?
pubcol-w-964e4c3f047fcece.example_complex: A skilled sommelier can tell the subtle differences between wines from neighbouring vineyards after a single sip.

0a7290d7-5ad9-44b4-b8f3-f508e00d76fc.definition_en: to moderate or hold back ambitious hopes so they become more realistic

c02e7069-a5bc-42e4-b9d3-7917bae2757e.definition_en: a person's natural character, especially how they typically feel and react

pubcol-w-4107f5f091bb9610.example_simple: I couldn't resist the temptation to eat another slice of cake.
pubcol-w-4107f5f091bb9610.example_complex: For many investors, the temptation to sell during a market panic is precisely what they must learn to overcome.

pubcol-w-99b0abd812ca7154.definition_en: so common and easy to find that it has little value
collocations: talent like that is ten a penny
such jobs are ten a penny
pubcol-w-99b0abd812ca7154.example_simple: Cheap souvenirs like these are ten a penny in tourist areas.
pubcol-w-99b0abd812ca7154.example_complex: Vague promises from politicians are ten a penny; what voters really want is concrete action.
